lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: email and message structure

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic email and message structure task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner picks one realistic scenario they might genuinely face, such as asking a coach, teacher, or activity leader a real question, and drafts a complete email following the four-part structure, without sending it to anyone since no real account or recipient is used in this task.
safetyNotes: This draft is never sent as part of the lesson; no real email account or recipient address is required.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific choice you made about tone or wording because you were writing to an adult outside your family rather than to a friend.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Structural completeness: All four parts are present and each clearly serves its function. | Clarity and tone: The single request is stated plainly, and the tone is appropriately professional. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner draft a second email for a different realistic scenario that requires declining a request rather than making one, using the same four-part structure.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic email and message structure task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: email and message structure worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner picks one realistic scenario they might genuinely face, such as asking a coach, teacher, or activity leader a real question, and drafts a complete email following the four-part structure, without sending it to anyone since no real account or recipient is used in this task.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact email and message structure decision or action.
Model move 2: Pick one realistic scenario where you would genuinely need to email an adult outside your family.
Model move 3: Draft your email using all four parts: a specific subject line, a greeting, a body with exactly one clearly stated request, and a closing with your name.

Model check: Structural completeness: All four parts are present and each clearly serves its function. | Clarity and tone: The single request is stated plainly, and the tone is appropriately professional.

resources.title: email and message structure action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for email and message structure.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: email and message structure coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner picks one realistic scenario they might genuinely face, such as asking a coach, teacher, or activity leader a real question, and drafts a complete email following the four-part structure, without sending it to anyone since no real account or recipient is used in this task.
Coach direction: Pick one realistic scenario where you would genuinely need to email an adult outside your family.
Learner prompt: Describe the scenario and the one specific thing you need from the recipient.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: email and message structure complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Draft your email using all four parts: a specific subject line, a greeting, a body with exactly one clearly stated request, and a closing with your name.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My subject line describes the specific topic, not a vague word like 'Question.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): My body states exactly one request in plain, direct language.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My closing includes my name and, if relevant, one identifying detail the recipient would need (such as which class or team).
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: email and message structure minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific choice you made about tone or wording because you were writing to an adult outside your family rather than to a friend.

Success checks: Structural completeness: All four parts are present and each clearly serves its function. | Clarity and tone: The single request is stated plainly, and the tone is appropriately professional.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: email and message structure supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional email and message structure condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Structural completeness: All four parts are present and each clearly serves its function. | Clarity and tone: The single request is stated plainly, and the tone is appropriately professional..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: email and message structure — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the email and message structure task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one specific choice you made about tone or wording because you were writing to an adult outside your family rather than to a friend.
observableCriteria: Structural completeness: All four parts are present and each clearly serves its function.
Clarity and tone: The single request is stated plainly, and the tone is appropriately professional.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Structural completeness: All four parts are present and each clearly serves its function. | Clarity and tone: The single request is stated plainly, and the tone is appropriately professional.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
